entries.content: I've been selling stuff on marketplace apps for about two years now. Honestly, I just text my address to buyers and have them come by. It's the same process I use when ordering food or packages - someone shows up, we exchange items, done. Saves so much time compared to coordinating meetup spots. Had maybe 40+ transactions this way with zero issues.

Sold the old bookshelf today. Met the buyer at the coffee shop parking lot on Main St. Took an extra 15 minutes out of my day but the transaction went smoothly. Buyer seemed nice enough but you never really know with strangers from the internet.

For convenience, many sellers share their address directly with buyers once payment is confirmed or agreed upon. This mirrors how you'd handle any home delivery - the person arrives, you hand over the item, and the transaction completes. Having the buyer come to you eliminates the hassle of transporting bulky items and coordinating schedules at third-party locations.

Address sharing for local transactions follows familiar patterns established by delivery services. When a buyer needs to collect an item, providing your location enables efficient completion of the sale. Sellers who handle multiple transactions often find home pickup reduces coordination overhead, particularly for larger items like furniture or electronics that are difficult to transport to alternate locations.

Finally sold my old gaming rig yesterday. Used the safe exchange spot at the police station - felt a bit awkward standing there with a PC tower but the buyer showed up on time. He tested it in his car for a few minutes before paying. Whole thing took longer than I wanted but at least everything went fine.
